# Illegal Saudi visa trade busted

KSA arrests 2 ex-officials of its Dhaka embassy, 2 officials of interior ministry, 8 Bangladeshis

Published : 5 March 2023

•

Updated : 6 March 2023, 09:34

• [DIPLOMACY](/news/bangladesh/diplomacy)

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

DIPLOMATIC CORRESPONDENT

![Saudi Arabia arrests 2 ex-officials](/sites/default/files/styles/big_1/public/images/2023/03/05/saudi_arabia-01.jpg)

The Saudi anti-corruption authority recently arrested four Saudi officials, eight Bangladeshis and a Palestinian on charges of corruption during issuance of visas for Bangladeshi migrant workers.

Among the arrestees are two diplomats, Abdullah Falah Mudhahi Al-Shammari and Khaled Nasser Ayed Al-Qahtani, who face charges of taking Tk 154 crore in exchange for finalising the issuance of work visas to Bangladeshis while they were working in Dhaka.

[Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source ![google-preferred-source-badge](/themes/custom/swallow/images/google_preferred_source_badge_dark.webp)](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thedailystar.net)

Al-Shammari was the deputy ambassador and Al-Qahtani was the  deputy head of the Consular Section at the Saudi embassy in Dhaka. Sources said both of them returned to the gulf country after they were suspended two months ago.

The Oversight and Anti-corruption Authority of Saudi Arabia, known in Arabic as Nazaha, yesterday tweeted: "They acknowledged receiving parts of the money from the arrested \[Bangladeshis\] residents inside Saudi Arabia and invested the rest outside the kingdom."

The authority initiated a criminal case into the matter.

The authority did not mention the exact time of the arrests.

The anti-corruption authority in coordination with the Saudi home ministry first arrested two officials of the ministry for "forcing a resident to sign a 23,000,000 SR financial commitment to a foreign investor" after taking SR 60,000 from the investor, Saleh Mohammed Saleh Al-Shalout of Palestine.

The arrested ministry officials are sergeant of the Court Security (Riyadh Police) Metab Saad Al-Ghnoum, and corporal of the Special Missions Forces in Riyadh Hatem Mastoor Saad bin Tayeb.

Upon further investigation, Bangladeshi expats Ashraf Uddin Aknad, Almgeer Hussain Khan, and Shafeeq Al Islam Shahjahan were arrested.

The three Bangladeshis, the Palestinian, and the two ministry officials admitted to engaging in illegal visa trading with the complicity of the employees of the Saudi embassy in Bangladesh.

"...By searching their homes, 20,180,000 SR \[about Tk 57.54 crore\] was found in cash, as well as gold ingots, and luxury vehicles, which turned out to be the proceeds of illegally selling work visas in the Kingdom," reads a tweet.

The other Bangladeshi arrestees are recruitment agency owner Mohammed Nasser Uddin Noor, and Al Ameen Khan, Zaid Uosied Mafy, Abul Kalam Mohammed Rafeeq Al Islam and Aziz Al Haq.

They were arrested for involvement in illegal visa trading and money smuggling outside the kingdom.

"Nazaha affirms on the continuation to pursue anyone who exploits the public office to achieve personal gain or harm public interest in any way, and that the accountability extends far beyond the retirement of individuals, as these types of crimes have no statute of limitations," it tweeted.

Saudi Ambassador to Bangladesh Essa Yousef did not comment when contacted by The Daily Star yesterday.

**HOW THE SCAM HAPPENED IN DHAKA**

Sources in Dhaka told this newspaper that three Saudi embassy officials were suspended around two months ago for taking bribes from recruiting agencies for issuing work visas. The third official who has not been arrested is yet to be identified.

The findings by the Saudi anti-graft body were corroborated by several international recruiting agents of Bangladesh.

According to them, the Saudi embassy in Dhaka about a year ago started charging recruiting agencies \$220 to \$250 for every work visa.

"The embassy suddenly set a rule that one recruiting agency would not be allowed to submit more than 20 visa applications a week and an agency would submit applications only once a week," a recruiting agent said.

#### [![Google News Link](/themes/custom/swallow/images/google_news.svg)For all latest news, follow The Daily Star's Google News channel.](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiECW73usLivqPCSeQRsSUvRQqFAgKIhAlu97rC4r6jwknkEbElL0U)

However, many agencies had several hundred passports to deal with. As they were desperate to have the work visas issued within a certain period, some individuals at the embassy started taking money.

"Thus, the visas were issued in exchange for money. Interestingly, we had to pay in dollars when there was a shortage of dollars in the country," a recruiting agent told The Daily Star.

The malpractice, however, stopped after the Saudi officials concerned were sent back to Saudi Arabia, the agent added.

Bangladesh's labour recruitment to Saudi Arabia surged phenomenally last year, with a total of 612,412 migrating to the kingdom. In the first two months of this year, 85,319 migrated there.

Interestingly, migrant remittance from the kingdom, where some 20 lakh Bangladeshis work, declined over the last two quarters.
